blocks.html:
What to know

  • Pyruvate dehydrogenase links glycolysis to the cycle. It converts pyruvate to acetyl-CoA and releases CO₂, producing NADH.
  • The cycle oxidizes acetyl groups. Citrate synthase condenses acetyl-CoA with oxaloacetate; the cycle returns to oxaloacetate after releasing two CO₂.
  • The yield per acetyl-CoA is 3 NADH, 1 FADH₂, and 1 GTP. The GTP is equivalent to ATP; the reduced carriers deliver electrons to the electron transport chain.
  • The cycle is amphibolic. It supplies intermediates for amino acids, heme, and fatty-acid synthesis, so anaplerotic reactions refill it.
  • Regulation matches energy demand. NADH and ATP inhibit pyruvate dehydrogenase and the cycle; ADP and NAD⁺ activate them.

Check

check.question: How many NADH are produced per acetyl-CoA in one turn of the TCA cycle?
check.explanation: One turn produces three NADH, one FADH₂, and one GTP, while releasing two CO₂.
